gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the "0.125 ms latency" Gamakay prints for the NS68 and Epomaker prints for the HE68 Lite and HE80 is the 8,000 Hz report interval itself (1 s / 8,000), that MCHOSE's 0.1 ms (Ace 60 Pro) and Gamakay's 0.06 ms (TK75HE V2) are shorter than one 8K report, or that Epomaker quotes 128K scan "per-key" on one board and "full board" on another.
standout_why: Compared against gamepadsquire, setupinsider, mechanicalkeyboard.net and hlplanet, which I read in full. The principle is already out there: mechanicalkeyboard.net says 8,000 Hz means one USB report every 0.125 ms, and ChatGPT's own answer repeats that (credited to keebforce). gamepadsquire already lists scan rates (HE68 Lite 128 kHz per-key, AULA 160 kHz single-key) and which boards are wired-only. What they lack is the per-model mapping: none says the makers' latency figure is that interval, none flags the two scan-rate bases, and none has a Gamakay row with numbers (hlplanet names NS68/NS75 without them). Three rival pages could not be checked: keebforce failed with a certificate error, and the pcgamer and rtings bodies came back as navigation only.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. On the makers' own numbers every sub-$100 candidate is level at 8,000 Hz wired, and the latency and scan-rate figures cannot rank them, so the choice falls to price, layout, rapid-trigger step and wireless. On maker-store prices read 2026-11-21 the Gamakay NS68 (65%, arrow keys, 0.01 mm) is $36.79, against $37.40 for the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro (60%) and $42.49 for the Epomaker HE68 Lite (65%). The NS75 and TK75HE V2 state a finer 0.005 mm step in 75%. MonsGeek's FUN60 Ultra is the only one whose maker states 8,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz as well as wired, but its page showed a pre-order notice. I could not read Gamakay's per-mode polling (store rate-limited), so the wireless comparison for Gamakay is open.
